question: A man with myopia magna, 47 years old, who underwent surgery for cataracts 2 years ago, goes to the emergency room referring to a profound and painless loss of vision in his right eye. Which of the following diagnoses can this symptom cause?

options.opc: Macular degeneration associated with age, wet form.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Myopia magna" -> "Increased risk of retinal detachment" -> "Retinal detachment" -> 80% CHAIN: "Cataract surgery" -> "Increased risk of posterior vitreous detachment" -> "Posterior vitreous detachment" -> 70% CHAIN: "Profound and painless loss of vision in right eye" -> "Possible retinal detachment" -> "Retinal detachment" -> 80%
analysis: Given the sudden and painless loss of vision in the right eye of a patient with a history of myopia magna and cataract surgery, the most likely diagnosis would be retinal detachment. This condition requires urgent evaluation and management to prevent permanent vision loss.
